footprint.measured: not measured: the footprint the run format draws for the NXT (libs/runfile adapters/nxt.py FOOTPRINT), nominal
footprint.why: a stand-in: the NXT has no navigator, so nothing plans with it; the block is here because today's profile schema requires one (NXT-D0.md section 3)

locomotion.measured: assumed, not measured (K16): a full track command is taken to be 0.3 m/s forward and 1.5 rad/s turning; D1 measures them at the brick
locomotion.why: what Mission Control turns a speed into a track command by (the nxt-web adapter's full_speed_mps and full_turn_rps, which a robot file may still set and which win): cruise_mps is both tracks at 100, yaw_max_rad_s the tracks 50 apart each way. A stand-in block: the NXT has no navigator to plan with it

capabilities.description: LEGO NXT 2.0 on tracks, behind nxt-web; no pose, no map, no navigator: status, drive and STOP only. Its speeds are not measured: locomotion.cruise_mps and yaw_max_rad_s are assumed values for a full track command

subsystems.name: nxt-web
subsystems.what: the connector: the only process on the brick's link; its lock, STOP and deadman are the robot's

subsystems.name: robotd-lite
subsystems.what: the program on the brick: the motors, the sensors, the stop when commands stop and the stop at 15 cm

subsystems.name: nxt-web
subsystems.what: the connector, run with --sim: the kinematic world, its ultrasonic and its stop at 15 cm stand in for the brick

capabilities.description: LEGO NXT 2.0 on tracks, behind nxt-web --sim (a kinematic world read from scene.json); the ultrasonic is simulated, the colour sensor is not (the scene has no floor colour). No pose, no map, no navigator: status, drive and STOP only
